categories.name: Landlord-tenant paralegals
categories.opportunity: Self-managing landlords who end up at the Landlord and Tenant Board over arrears or a difficult tenancy often decide afterward that they do not want to manage the property themselves again.
categories.rationale: The paralegal meets the owner at peak frustration and is asked, 'How do I stop this happening again?' You can refer your own tribunal files to them in return.

triggers.event: A self-managing landlord files for arrears or termination
triggers.whyNeed: They need better tenant screening and ongoing management
triggers.partnerValue: Their client avoids a repeat case

triggers.event: A managed tenancy needs a tribunal application
triggers.partnerValue: Steady, well-documented files for the paralegal

categories.mutualValue: Paralegals gain a steady flow of well-documented files; you gain owners ready to delegate.
categories.approach: Send your tribunal work to one or two landlord-side paralegals and ask them to share your information with clients who want ongoing help.
categories.decisionMaker: Paralegal who represents landlords at the tribunal
categories.regulatoryNote: Paralegals are law society licensees with referral-fee rules. Keep the arrangement non-compensated.

categories.name: Realtors with investor buyers
categories.opportunity: An investor buying a rental needs a rent estimate before buying and a tenant-placement plan at closing. Agents who work with investors are asked for manager recommendations repeatedly.
categories.rationale: A single investor-focused agent can produce several new management contracts a year, and your rent analysis helps them sell properties.

triggers.event: An investor makes an offer on a rental property
triggers.whyNeed: They need realistic rent and expense assumptions
The unit must be leased or the existing tenancy taken over

categories.mutualValue: Agents gain rent analyses that help them sell; you gain new doors at closing.
categories.approach: Offer free rent assessments on investment listings and a guaranteed lease-up plan for agents' buyers.
categories.decisionMaker: Buyer's agent who works with investors
categories.regulatoryNote: Real estate registrants may not pay referral fees to non-registrants. Keep the relationship non-compensated unless both parties are registered and the rules are met.

categories.name: Estate lawyers & executors
categories.opportunity: Estates often hold tenanted rentals or vacant homes during administration, and executors, who frequently live elsewhere, must protect the asset. Vacant properties may also face insurance conditions such as regular inspections.
categories.rationale: Executors have a fiduciary duty and little time, so professional management solves a real problem, sometimes for months or years.

triggers.event: An estate includes a tenanted rental
triggers.whyNeed: Rent collection, maintenance, and tenancy obligations continue
triggers.partnerValue: Protects the estate and the executor's duty

triggers.event: An estate home sits vacant pending sale
triggers.whyNeed: Insurance and security conditions require oversight

categories.mutualValue: Executors meet their duties with documented oversight; you gain interim and long-term contracts.
categories.approach: Offer an estate-property service (inspections, rent collection, sale preparation) and introduce it to estate lawyers.
categories.decisionMaker: Executor (often advised by the estate lawyer)

assumptions: Property-management contracts usually change hands at a moment of pain or transition: a purchase, a bad tenant, an inheritance, a move, or a lender stepping in. The professionals present at those moments are the strongest sources.
Your vendor network is both a cost centre and a referral network. Trades see self-managing owners struggle long before those owners call a manager.
No typical project value was provided, so commercial-value ratings are relative to the industry, not your own pricing.

guardrails.title: Licensing and conflicts of interest
guardrails.body: In Ontario, leasing on behalf of owners for compensation is generally regulated real estate activity, and condominium management requires a separate licence. Real estate registrants may not pay referral fees to non-registrants. As an agent of owners, disclose any vendor rebates or referral arrangements to your clients. Confirm your obligations with the relevant regulators.

guardrails.title: Partnerships are not paid-referral arrangements
guardrails.body: This analysis recommends building relationships based on mutual value. It does not assume that referral fees, commissions, exclusivity, or endorsements are permitted in your industry. Check professional, regulatory, and contractual rules before compensating anyone for referrals.

guardrails.title: Outreach in Canada: CASL applies
guardrails.body: Commercial electronic messages generally need express or implied consent, sender identification, and a working unsubscribe mechanism. Implied consent can exist when a business email address is conspicuously published, the message relates to the recipient's role, and they have not said they don't want such messages. Keep records of how consent was obtained. Personal information you collect is also subject to privacy law (e.g. PIPEDA).

guardrails.title: No automated outreach
guardrails.body: This tool does not contact anyone on your behalf. Every introduction should be personal, relevant to the recipient, and easy to decline.
